references.text: Jesus uses a similar image in [ref:Matt 17:20|Matthew 17:20], where he says that faith like a mustard seed can move mountains. Both the mustard seed as a symbol of the smallest faith and the impossible becoming possible through faith are common themes.

In [ref:Matt 21:21|Matthew 21:21], Jesus again speaks about the power of faith to do what seems impossible, such as casting a mountain into the sea, which reflects the promise about the mulberry tree being uprooted and planted in the sea.

In [ref:Mark 11:22-23|Mark 11:22-23], Jesus encourages the disciples to have faith in God and says that whoever believes can tell a mountain to throw itself into the sea, and it will happen. This is a parallel to the promise about the power of faith in Luke 17:6.

In [ref:Matt 13:31-32|Matthew 13:31-32], Jesus uses the mustard seed (κόκκον σινάπεως) as an image in the parable of the kingdom of heaven—the smallest of all seeds that grows into a large tree. The same image of something very small is used in Luke 17:6 regarding faith.

Paul mentions in [ref:1 Kor 13:2|1 Corinthians 13:2] that even if one has all faith, so as to move mountains, but does not have love, one is nothing. This refers to the same idea of a faith that can do the impossible.

[ref:Luk 17:5|Luke 17:5] is the immediate context where the apostles ask the Lord: "Increase our faith!" Jesus' answer in verse 6 shows that it is not about the size of faith, but about its presence and authenticity.

In [ref:Jak 5:15|James 5:15], it states that the prayer of faith will save the sick. This emphasizes the same point as Luke 17:6: that even a basic, sincere faith has great power and can accomplish mighty things.
